change_regions.change: FIFO-only reset uses xpm_cdc_sync_rst with four clk_fast stages. The signal fifo_reset is the only FIFO.rst driver.
Three explicitly initialized reset-state bits and two two-stage CDC level synchronizers implement FIFO completion -> slow ready -> fast admission.
Both busy outputs immediately include common_reset and remain asserted until their reset-handshake release condition.
FIFO.rst changes from rst_fast to fifo_reset.
Fast state/credit alignment and slow state reset now use the complete domain busy conditions instead of only the raw FIFO busy flag.

xpm_api_review.meaning: The destination register chain initializes to 1 and clocks the entire src_rst level, so normal assertion and deassertion both occur after clk_fast edges. INIT_SYNC_FF=1 additionally models GSR initialization in simulation. It is not a single-stage asynchronous sample.
xpm_api_review.handshake_configuration: Each xpm_cdc_single uses DEST_SYNC_FF=2, INIT_SYNC_FF=1, SRC_INPUT_REG=0, SIM_ASSERT_CHK=1; both source levels are registered. Their initial synchronized outputs are 0.

correctness_argument: common_reset remains a direct asynchronous mask in both domain busy outputs, preventing new input acceptance, FIFO read/write and output validity immediately. Existing local asynchronous-assert/synchronous-release resets are retained.

After an externally captured reset request, rst_fast remains asserted across four fast edges. FIFO reset passes through four further clocked stages; the pulse is therefore not presented asynchronously to XPM_FIFO_ASYNC.rst. This does not promise capture of a pulse below hardware minimum width.

fifo_reset_done cannot assert before fifo_reset_seen, which requires observing fifo_reset && wr_busy. Completion then requires both fifo_reset and wr_busy low. The reviewed XPM 2021.1 wr_busy remains high through both internal reset passes.

slow_reset_ready remains zero until the synchronized completion level arrives and local rd_busy is low. Therefore a temporary rd_busy low interval between the two reset passes cannot admit reads or backend work.
Fast input admission waits for the slow-ready acknowledgement to return through two fast stages, so no new packet can reach a slow domain still held in reset.
The handshake has no cyclic release dependency: FIFO completion depends only on local FIFO state; slow ready depends on completion/rd_busy; final fast admission depends on returned ready.

The fast control busy branch continuously aligns done_seen with done_sync, while the slow busy branch holds done_toggle at zero. Asynchronous reset clears the reset-handshake source levels and four-edge local tails allow the two-stage synchronizers to flush; old credit cannot reopen a new frame during reset.

The three new register initial values, INIT=1 FIFO reset, and initialized handshake synchronizers keep primary ready/valid interfaces closed at GSR-only startup. Existing busy branches initialize control before admission; payload registers may be unspecified while valid is zero.

independent_review.final_change_after_independent_review: Only line 25 comment changed to state that a pulse must first be captured; logic unchanged.

minimum_required_validation: After initialization/GSR, every fifo_reset assertion and deassertion must coincide with a clk_fast edge; distinguish sampled pre-edge values from post-NBA changes.
No accepted input or FIFO write while fast_reset_busy; no FIFO read/backend input/output handshake while slow_reset_busy. Check both enables throughout both FIFO reset passes.
No fifo_reset_done before seen reset+writer-busy and complete writer-busy removal; no slow-ready before synchronized completion and rd_busy low; no fast admission before returned slow-ready.
Observe credit reset/alignment and prove no stale read/result/frame appears after reset/abort at queued, drained partial, FFT-output and held-result cancellation.

Root-selected R1 link regression preserves the 22 normal F + 10 link-error E + 8 discard D matrix and requires 32 true H retirements; add only reset-edge and domain-busy IO observations. Do not independently rerun completed 001-009 jobs.
Record startup and near-release reset behavior separately from physical minimum-pulse or metastability qualification.
boundaries: This RTL and report are an unfrozen draft pending the next revision freeze and native validation. No compile, simulation or timing success is claimed.

The clock inputs must run continuously. Per the XPM contract, a new external reset should not be issued before both busy outputs from the previous reset sequence deassert. Holding one reset request high is supported.
An external pulse must satisfy the physical capture/minimum-pulse requirements of the asynchronous reset path. RTL pulse stretching is not proof for arbitrarily narrow physical pulses.

A reset immediately adjacent to a newly asserted reset-ready/done level can interrupt the XPM single-bit stable-for-two-following-samples assumption. Capture these reset levels if such a corner is tested; do not silently suppress unrelated S-1 diagnostics.

At GSR-only startup read_audit_valid may remain X before the first slow clock because the original bare register has no initializer; consumers must qualify audit with slow_reset_busy. Primary ready/valid interfaces are masked.
The 18 previous XPM model diagnostics and precompiled binding are separate root-owned work. This draft does not edit vendor assertions, simulation library mapping, old XPR, Tcl or TB.
Root will separately freeze any private simulation-only checker corrections and explicit private cfo_xpm library. Those changes are not included here.
No physical CDC, implementation timing, sustained-throughput, board or whole T11/T12/T13 acceptance follows from this static review.
